sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Now I see something very interesting! After rotating the room LEFT and then SPACE with purple:
- id=13: purple, 55 pixels, boundary [[34, 27], [34, 36], [43, 27]] - this is a triangular shape (purple on the left/top)
- id=14: white, 45 pixels, boundary [[35, 36], [43, 36], [43, 28]] - this is a triangular shape (white on the right/bottom)
The bottom block is now split diagonally! The rotation of the room determines the split direction:
- Room in center (rectangular): horizontal split (top/bottom)
- Room rotated LEFT (diagonal): diagonal split
Looking at the image, the bottom block now has a diagonal split: purple on the upper-left and white on the lower-right.
So the room's orientation determines how the bottom block is split! Let me think about what orientations give what splits:
- Center (rectangular): horizontal split
- LEFT (diagonal): diagonal split (upper-left / lower-right)
- RIGHT (diagonal): probably another diagonal split (upper-right / lower-left)
- DOWN (lower-rectangular): maybe vertical split?
The reference pattern is white (top) + purple (bottom) - a horizontal split. So I need the room in the center position.
But the problem is: when the room is in center position and I SPACE with a color, the split is: selected color on top, original color on bottom. To get white on top, purple on bottom, I need:
- Bottom block merged purple
- SPACE with white selected
- Result: white on top, purple on bottom
But I can't get a merged purple block because:
- From merged white, SPACE(purple) → split (purple top, white bottom)
- From split (purple top, white bottom), SPACE(purple) → no change
- From split (purple top, white bottom), SPACE(white) → merged white
So there's no way to get merged purple from merged white using SPACE alone. Unless... I use a different orientation to do something, then rotate back.
Wait, let me think about this differently. When the room is rotated LEFT and I SPACE with purple:
- The bottom block is split diagonally: purple (upper-left, 55 pixels) + white (lower-right, 45 pixels)
What if I SPACE with white when the room is rotated LEFT?
- Maybe it merges to white?
- Or maybe it does something else?
Let me try: SPACE with white when room is rotated LEFT.
